name: Butt Bridge
facts: The original Butt Bridge, opened 26 August 1879, was a 200‑ton wrought‑iron swing span powered by a steam engine, allowing boats to pass as far upstream as Carlisle Bridge.
In 1932, the swing bridge was replaced by a three‑span reinforced‑concrete structure, the first in Britain or Ireland to use cantilevered and counter‑weight construction in concrete.
Named after Isaac Butt, the bridge’s Irish title Droichead na Comhdhála commemorates the 1932 Eucharistic Congress held in Dublin.
